newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm on China demand, crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm on China demand, crude.

text.p: Expectations for fresh demand from China supported the high sulphur fuel oil market on Monday although trading was thin after the three-day weekend, traders said.
Two bids, both for late April delivery, for the 180-cst grade were heard at $100.50 and $100.00 respectively but failed to find suppliers.
"Demand is quite healthy but with Europe on holiday today and after the long weekend, not much trading interest is there," said one trader.
Healthy demand from a local trader late last week supported prices above $100 and a local trading company was heard moving three cargoes to China over the weekend, traders said.
"Suppliers are waiting for prices to go up also over crude gains," the trader added.

Late on Thursday, two bids for 15,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade, 3.5-percent and 15,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade, 0.5 percent fuel oil, both to South China, emerged, fueling hopes for fresh Chinese demand.

"It seems demand from China is picking up," said one trader. Recent fuel oil purchase by Taiwan and India also inspired sentiment, as well as the low level of Singapore residue stocks which fell by 1.096 million barrels to 10.664 milllion barrels in the week ending March 26, traders said.
Despite the overall optimism, most traders agreed that current supplies remained sufficient and could limit the upward momentum.
In the LSWR market, the Korean Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) has awarded its tender to buy 500,000 barrels of LSWR to Dutch trader Vitol.
The cargo for delivery between May 11-15 to the ports of Ulsan or Pusan is awarded at $18.55 per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
